summary: Exfoliating toner that many users say smooths texture, clears pores and brightens, and a large share use it on the body, scalp or underarms. On the face, irritation and stinging are the main complaints, with breakouts for some, and many limit it to once or twice a week. Some also find it sticky.

Cheap serum that many users credit with less oil, clearer pores and more even tone. The main complaint is breakouts, followed by irritation and stinging for a good number of users. Some find it sticky or prone to pilling under moisturizer or makeup, and many tolerate it better as a few drops mixed into moisturizer.

Short-contact peel that many users say leaves skin smoother, brighter and clearer, usually used weekly or less. Irritation and stinging are the main complaints, and many apply it to dry skin for only a few minutes. A few feel nothing or see little change, and several prefer it on feet.

Leave-on exfoliant that many users credit with clearing clogged pores and blackheads and smoothing texture, often used just a few times a week. Some find it irritating or drying, a smaller group break out, and several dislike an oily, tacky film. Tolerance varies, even among sensitive skin types.

Non-foaming, creamy cleanser that many users find very gentle and comfortable on dry or sensitive skin, often preferring it to CeraVe's. The biggest complaint is burning or stinging for a sizable group, sometimes starting with a new bottle, plus irritation or breakouts for others. Some feel it does not clean well enough alone.

Soothing, rich balm that many users use on dry, irritated or barrier-stressed skin, often at night or alongside tretinoin. The main downside is breakouts for a good number of users, especially with oily or acne-prone skin, plus a heavy, greasy feel. Several say a newer formula is drier or less effective.

Glowy, tinted sunscreen that fans wear as a radiant primer or light base, with little white cast. Many others find it greasy or too shimmery, and breakouts are a frequent complaint, along with pilling over moisturizer or makeup. Some say the tint looks orange or metallic on them, and a few report it separating.

Lightweight, sticky gel cream that many users find hydrating and gentle, and it seems to suit oily or combination skin and warmer weather. A common caveat is that it is not enough alone for dry skin, so many layer a richer cream over it. A smaller group reports breakouts or irritation.

Gooey, hydrating essence that many users love for soft, plump skin, and some say it calms redness. The main downside is breakouts, mostly small closed bumps, for a fair number of users, with some reporting stinging or dryness. Some layer a moisturizer over it.

Gentle, non-foaming cleanser that many users say leaves dry and sensitive skin comfortable and not tight. Some get breakouts or irritation from it, and several feel it leaves a film or does not clean well, especially for makeup or sunscreen on its own. Best seen as a mild morning or second cleanse.

Rich, hydrating cream that many users with dry skin love, usually as a night or winter moisturizer. Downsides are breakouts for some and a heavy, greasy feel, especially on oily skin or in humid weather. A noticeable fragrance bothers a few, while a small amount goes a long way.

Light, fast-absorbing lotion that many users find hydrating and gentle, and some wear it morning and night. The main complaint is breakouts, often closed comedones, for a good number of users. Some find it not moisturizing enough for very dry skin, and a few noticed a different feel or irritation after a reformulation.

Cheap eye serum that many users say reduces morning puffiness, though the effect is usually temporary. Results for dark circles are mixed, and dryness or irritation under the eyes is the main complaint. A few mention pilling under makeup or eye twitching, and many add moisturizer or eye cream over it.

Budget cleansing balm that many users find gentle and soothing, and several say it melts makeup and sunscreen well as a first cleanse. Downsides are a greasy film that needs a second cleanse, breakouts or eye irritation for some, and a hard-to-squeeze tube with texture that can separate or turn grainy.

Thick but easy-spreading cream that many users with dry, sensitive skin find hydrating and calming, especially in winter. The main complaints are irritation, stinging or burning for some, often blamed on eucalyptus oil, and breakouts for others. A few say a formula change stopped it working for them.

Moisturizer with sunscreen that a few users like as a lightweight one-step product, but pilling is the main complaint, with many describing it balling up alone or under makeup. Breakouts, a greasy feel and a visible white cast also come up, and several switched to the PM lotion or a separate sunscreen.

Light, cooling gel that many users with oily or combination skin find hydrating without greasiness. The main complaint is breakouts, followed by irritation and a strong scent in the regular version, with several preferring the fragrance-free one. Dry skin usually needs a richer cream on top, and a few report eyelid reactions.

Very lightweight sunscreen serum that many users like for a dewy finish, little white cast and enough moisture to skip a moisturizer. Breakouts and stinging, mostly around the eyes, are the main complaints for a smaller group, and some find it shiny on oily skin. Several say newer bottles feel different.

Light, gel-like moisturizer that many users with oily or combination skin like for daytime and under makeup. Price is a recurring complaint, and some find it too light for dry skin. A smaller group got breakouts or a shiny, greasy look.

Thick, soothing cream that many users use on irritated, redness-prone skin and while using retinoids, and several prefer it to Cicaplast. The main downside is clogged pores and breakouts for a good number of users, and some find it too greasy or heavy, especially in summer.

Most users like it as a lightweight, hydrating day moisturizer that sits well under sunscreen and makeup, and several have repurchased it. A few found it not moisturizing enough on its own or at night, and a few broke out or saw no effect. It is described as expensive.

Many users find it a light, hydrating gel cream that does not pill under sunscreen, especially in warm or humid weather. The main downside is breakouts: several got bumps or clogged pores within days, which stopped when they quit it. One had an allergic reaction. Layering other creams over it can pill.

Users are split. Some find it soothing and hydrating, helpful for dry skin or irritation from actives like tretinoin. Others got burning, redness or breakouts, sometimes after only a few uses, and a few saw pilling under other products or disliked the smell. Sensitive and acne-prone skin seem to be the riskiest.

Many users credit it with clearing blackheads and breakouts without drying skin, and some use it daily. Others saw no effect or got breakouts, and a few had irritation or a rash. Some noticed a strong chemical smell in newer bottles.

Most users love it as a moisturizing, barrier-repairing layer that leaves skin dewy and helps dry or flaky skin. The main downside is irritation, mostly from people sensitive to its niacinamide. One found the smell like fish oil, and one said it is too costly to import.

Most users like it as a hydrating, quick-absorbing serum that plumps and smooths skin, with little irritation and some long-term daily users. Downsides are mixed: some saw no real results, found it sticky or greasy, or disliked the renamed formula. A couple reported hair changes they linked to it.

Many users say it clears closed comedones and bumps and find it gentler than other AHAs. The main complaint is the smell, which several dislike. Some got breakouts, stinging or irritation, and a few saw results plateau or fade over time.

Most users rate it among the best pimple patches, good at drawing out gunk and flattening pimples overnight, and it sticks well. Several note it works best on open or surfaced spots and not on deep cystic ones. A few found it ineffective and preferred other brands such as Nexcare.

Many users see brightening and a more even tone, and some call it the most effective vitamin C they have tried. The main complaint is a strong, unpleasant smell. A few found it stinging, drying or too irritating, and some saw no results.

Users are split. Some enjoy it as a lightweight, hydrating, calming essence and have repurchased it. Many others noticed no effect or found it only mildly hydrating, and a few found it greasy, sticky or irritating.

Most users find it a very gentle AHA that smooths texture and evens skin without irritation, even on sensitive skin or alongside tretinoin. Several say it cleared stubborn closed comedones. A couple of people broke out or found it not strong enough.

Reviews from users are split. Some with sturdy or dry skin find it gentle and pore-smoothing, and it plays well with other actives. The main complaint is irritation, with several reporting a damaged barrier or breakouts, and a few found it too weak to exfoliate.

Many users see brightening and a more even tone from this strong vitamin C. The main downsides are a greasy, gritty texture, and stinging for some, plus pilling under other products or makeup. It is described as potent and not for beginners.

Most users broke out, some severely, with bumps, whiteheads or cystic acne that cleared after stopping. A few liked how it lifts oil and sebum from pores without a greasy film. The breakout reports outweigh the praise in these reviews.

Many users like it as a light gel-cream that absorbs fast and calms redness, and a few call it a holy grail. The main downside is that it is not moisturizing enough for cold or dry weather. Some found it sticky or pilling, and one broke out.

Most users love it as a gentle cleanser that leaves skin soft and not stripped, and several call it a holy grail. A couple found it harsh or barrier-damaging, and one felt the reformulation cleanses less well.

Most users find them a gentle exfoliant that improves texture and evens skin tone, including some with sensitive skin when used once or twice a week. Some got redness or irritation, and one found them ineffective. One mentions a purge early on and that they feel pricey.

Most users find it a simple, soothing, hydrating serum that works for sensitive or dry, barrier-damaged skin and sits well under makeup. Downsides are mixed: a few got irritation, allergic bumps or eczema, one found it now stings, and some felt it does little beyond hydrate.

Its main issue is irritation: many users got peeling or burns, even experienced retinol users, and often need to buffer it or use it only a few nights a week. A few use it long-term with good results or clearer acne, while others saw no effect. Best treated as a strong retinol to start slowly.

Most users find it a gentle salicylic cleanser that helps with acne, blackheads and oil, and some use it daily for years. Downsides include dryness or peeling with long use, and a couple of people got irritation or burns. One noted a strong perfume smell in a newer bottle.

Most users find it a gentle exfoliating toner that smooths texture, calms congestion and fades marks, with some on their third bottle. A few found it irritating, stinging or ineffective, and one blamed it for a compromised barrier. Some tolerate it well even with acid-sensitive skin.

Users' reviews are split. Some like it as a light, good-value cream that de-puffs and tightens under the eyes, and a few have repurchased. Many saw no effect or found it nothing special, it did not help dark circles, and a few found it stinging, harsh or pilling.

Most users like how light and non-greasy it feels, with no white cast and a gentle feel on sensitive or acne-prone skin. The complaints are spread out: pilling over moisturizer or under makeup, breakouts for some, and stinging or irritation for others. A few report a bad smell or a formula change.

Most users find it a gentle, low-key retinol that suits sensitive skin, with many reporting clearer skin, smoother texture and a more even tone. Some break out or purge for a long time, a few get dryness or irritation, and others find it too mild to do much. A reasonable starter retinol.

Most users like it as a light, quick-absorbing gel that hydrates without clogging, including on oily or acne-prone skin. The main downsides are pilling under sunscreen or other products and irritation for some sensitive skin. A few find it not moisturizing enough for dry skin or dislike the smell.

Most users find it gentle and hydrating, with many seeing calmer redness, a more even tone and fewer breakouts, including on sensitive skin. Some feel it does nothing or stopped working over time, a few break out, and several find it sticky. Better for redness and general acne than stubborn marks.

Most users love it as a light, comfortable sunscreen with no white cast and a velvety or satin finish, especially on oily and combination skin. The downsides are a smell some dislike, breakouts for a few, and a slightly greasy or sweaty look on some. Many name it a favorite.

Users lean negative. Many report breakouts or clogged pores, and many more find it drying, stripping or irritating, sometimes with stinging. A smaller group finds it gentle, non-stripping and good at removing makeup, mainly on oily or combination skin.

Most users find it a watery, lightweight ampoule that calms redness and helps a stressed barrier, often alongside tretinoin or other actives. Some break out or get irritated, and a few notice nothing from it. It suits sensitive, redness-prone skin best.

Most users use it as a night occlusive or for chapped lips and dry, irritated skin, and many prefer it to Aquaphor or Vaseline. It is rich and can feel sticky. A handful say the newer formula feels waxy or tacky or caused stinging and redness.

Most users like it as a light, cooling, gel-like moisturizer that hydrates and absorbs quickly, especially on oily or combination skin and in warm, humid weather. Dry skin and winter often need something richer. A few break out, find it sticky, or see it pill.

Users are split. Many see dark spots and acne marks fade and tone even out, especially fresh marks, while others saw little change on older spots. Breakouts are the most common complaint, with several linking them to niacinamide. The gel texture is light and absorbs quickly.

Most users love it as a hydrating, gentle toner, and many have repurchased it. The scent is the main complaint, described as candy-like or cucumbery. A few find it does little, pills under makeup, or caused breakouts or flaking.

Most users rely on it as a thick, fragrance-free cream for sensitive or irritated skin, often at night or over tretinoin, and like the good value. It is slow to absorb and can sit on top. A few find it too occlusive or say it broke them out.

Most users find it rich, hydrating and soothing without feeling greasy, and it helps dry or irritated skin, including on tretinoin. A few broke out or felt stinging, some link this to niacinamide. A few dislike the small jar.

Reviews from users lean negative. Breakouts and clogged pores are the most common complaint, followed by irritation, and several say the reformulated bottle smells odd, feels greasier or stings. Some long-time users still find it hydrating enough for very dry skin and a reliable staple.

Most users find it very hydrating, lightweight and quick to absorb, without stickiness or scent. Some feel it does little beyond basic hydration and want a cream on top. A few broke out, and a couple found it useless.

Most users find it a gentle, lotion-like cleanser for sensitive or reactive skin, including on tretinoin or during eczema flares. Several long-time users say the reformulated version irritated them, smelled bad or broke them out. Some with oily skin find it tight or not cleansing enough.

Most users like it as a cheap, long-lasting cleanser that cleans without feeling squeaky, and many call it a staple. The main downside is dryness or tightness, with irritation for some sensitive skin. A few mention a tea tree smell.

Most users find it a hydrating, gentle toner that absorbs well, gives a glow and calms redness, with some saying it helped acne. It is slightly thick but not sticky. A couple had irritation, and a few noted newer bottles smelling off or thinner.

Users' opinions are divided. Some say it helps blackheads and congested pores, especially left on for a couple of minutes. More users report breakouts, dryness or irritation instead. Suited to those who tolerate salicylic acid washes.

Most users are happy with it, reporting clearer skin, fewer marks and good tolerance even on sensitive skin. Several get pilling under sunscreen or moisturizer, and a few break out or react, some blaming its added salicylic acid. A few saw no change.

Users' opinions are mixed. Several find it a gentle BHA that smooths texture and helps blackheads, and it suits some sensitive skin. A larger group saw no difference on blackheads or closed comedones, and some report breakouts or more clogged pores.

Most users find it very gentle, removing makeup and sunscreen without stinging or sticky residue, even on rosacea or acne-prone skin. Some report irritation or breakouts, and a few say newer bottles stung their eyes. Mineral or tinted sunscreen may need a second pass.

Most users find the Laneige Water Sleeping Mask hydrating and light, with a dewy, non-greasy feel that locks in the layers under it. It splits opinion: some say it is too thin and not occlusive enough for dry skin, and a few dislike the scent. It suits those wanting a light final step rather than a rich overnight cream.

Most users find the CeraVe Ultra-Light Moisturizing Lotion SPF 30 truly lightweight, fast-absorbing and free of white cast, with a soft matte finish that sits well under makeup. A few found it greasy or were broken out by it. It is especially liked by oily and combination skin.

Many users find the Beauty of Joseon Revive Eye Serum gentle for a retinal, using it around the eyes or over the face with slow, subtle improvement in fine lines and under-eye texture. Irritation is the main downside, with several reporting dryness, itching, swelling or gritty eyes. Dark circles often change little.

Most users like the COSRX Aloe Soothing Sun Cream SPF 50 for its hydrating, gentle feel and lack of white cast, and many save it for winter or cooler days. The fragrance is the most common complaint, and some find it too rich, oily or stinging near the eyes. A few reported pilling under makeup.

Many users say the Beauty of Joseon Glow Deep Serum evens skin tone and fades dark marks and post-acne discoloration, often noticeable after weeks. Others saw only hydration or no change, and some find it tacky. A few broke out, so results look uneven, but it is generally gentle.

Most users find the Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Hyaluronic Toner hydrating, light and not sticky, and many tolerate it well even with sensitive skin. The main downside is breakouts, with several reporting new bumps or closed comedones despite it feeling good. A few found it did little.

Users are split on Drunk Elephant Lala Retro Whipped Cream. Fans find it rich, moisturizing and gentle, even on sensitive skin or over tretinoin. Others find it greasy, slow to sink in or irritating, some saw breakouts, and several say it is not worth the price. Not a sure thing, and skin type seems to matter.

Most users find the COSRX The 6 Peptide Skin Booster Serum nicely hydrating but unremarkable, often comparing it to a hydrating toner with no clear anti-aging effect, and many are unsure they would repurchase. Some do see smoother, plumper skin, and it is gentle for many. A few reported breakouts.

Most users love Supergoop! Mineral Mattescreen SPF 40 for oily and combination skin, describing a primer-like, mattifying finish with a slight tint that works well under makeup. Some find it drying, so a moisturizer underneath may help, and a few dislike the scent or broke out. Some call it pricey.

Most users love Avène Thermal Spring Water as a calming mist, using it after washing, midday, while traveling or on irritated and flushed skin. Gentle is the top praise, with a satisfying spray. A couple found it did little or even dried and irritated their skin, and one called it expensive water.

Most users find Torriden SOLID-IN Ceramide Cream rich but fast-absorbing, fragrance-free and good for dry skin and barrier support, including during tretinoin use. Some found it more occlusive than hydrating or too rich, and a few reacted or broke out, notably after a reformulation. Better for dry skin than oily.

Many users love EltaMD UV Physical SPF 41 as a lightweight tinted mineral sunscreen, especially very fair users, with a satin finish and no sting. Downsides are mixed: some find it greasy, drying or orange, a few broke out or saw pilling, and one dislikes the reformulation. The tint suits light skin best.

Most users praise KraveBeauty Great Barrier Relief as a gentle, healing barrier product that calms sensitivity and works alongside tretinoin, with many calling it a holy grail. Some had irritation, redness or a breakout, and a few found it not moisturizing enough alone. It suits reactive skin, though a few reacted badly.

Most users love numbuzin No.3 Super Glowing Essence Toner for hydration and a glowy, smoother look, with a pleasant if fairly strong scent. Irritation is the main downside, with several reporting itching, redness or a reaction, so it can be too much for reactive skin. Some use it only a few times a week.

Most users find the Beauty of Joseon Green Plum Refreshing Cleanser very gentle and non-stripping, leaving skin soft with a light foam. A few felt it stripped, did not clean well enough, or led to clogged pores, and some say it did little. It suits those who want a mild cleanser.

Users, many of them loyal users for a decade or more, find First Aid Beauty Pure Skin Face Cleanser gentle and effective for sensitive skin, and a little goes a long way. The main downsides are a reformulation that disappoints some and a scent that a few find off. One found it drying.

Users are split on Drunk Elephant T.L.C. Framboos Glycolic Night Serum. Fans find it a gentle acid that brightens, smooths texture and evens tone, even on sensitive skin. Others saw no difference, dryness, stinging or breakouts, and several say it is pricey. It works well for some and not at all for others.

Most users like the Beauty of Joseon Red Bean Refreshing Pore Mask as a gentle clay-style mask that leaves skin soft without drying, with many noticing clearer nose blackheads and smaller-looking pores. It is good value. A few saw purging, redness or breakouts, and some saw no change.

Most users like The INKEY List Hyaluronic Acid Serum as a cheap, lightweight serum that sinks in without stickiness, and many prefer it to The Ordinary's version. A few found it irritating or not hydrating enough, including a newer bottle that bothered a long-term user. Good value for simple hydration.

Most users find Byoma Milky Toner very hydrating and soft-feeling, and many have rebought it several times, including those with dry or Accutane-affected skin. Some reacted with burning, redness or breakouts, and a few felt newer bottles differ. Gentle for many, but not for everyone.

Users who like Supergoop! PLAY Everyday Lotion SPF 50 find it moisturizing, with no white cast and a healthy dewy finish that works under makeup. The scent is the most common complaint, described as citrusy or strong, and some found it shiny, sticky or stinging near the eyes. A few broke out.

Most users find it a very hydrating, gentle milky toner that suits dry, sensitive and even oily skin, and several call it a long-term staple. A couple of people found it irritating, heavy or useless in winter.

Most users use it as an overnight spot treatment and see pimples noticeably smaller by morning, especially whiteheads. It is less effective on deep or cystic spots, can stop working for some, and may burn sensitive skin.

Most users like it: it absorbs fast without pilling, keeps skin balanced and clear, and a few note faded marks. A noticeable minority broke out from it, so the high niacinamide level clearly doesn't suit everyone.

Most users find it a light, hydrating oil that sensitive and even oily or eczema-prone skin tolerates well without greasiness or clogging. A few disliked it, with one saying it worsened eczema and another noting an off smell.

Users split on this thick, hydrating cream: some find it deeply moisturizing and soothing for dry or damaged skin, while others say it sits on top of the skin or feels occlusive. The bergamot scent bothers several, and a few found it irritating.

Most users like this light gel cream, especially on oily or acne-prone skin, and some use it as a long-term holy grail. The main downside is that several people say a newer bottle looks different and broke them out. Dry, sensitive skin found it greasy or tingly.

Users describe a very rich, moisturizing ceramide cream that many find repairing and cooling, including on sensitive skin. Its richness is too heavy for some, a few reacted with congestion, burning or breakouts, and several say a restocked version feels different.

Many users find it hydrating and gentle, even for sensitive or rosacea-prone skin, and some call it a long-term favorite. Several, though, developed small bumps or breakouts, and a few found it sticky, heavy or irritating. Its mild exfoliating effect is felt by some.

Most users love this serum, describing a plump, glowy look and gentle behavior even on very sensitive or reactive skin. It suits dry, oily and combination types alike. One user broke out, and one notes the results are temporary.

Most users like it, especially on dry or sensitive skin, saying it brightens and evens tone with a nice lotion-like texture. A couple found it too greasy or broke out from it, and one thought the bottle underfilled.

Users mostly find a mineral sunscreen with a mild white cast that fades and a calming, lotion-like feel. The earthy mugwort scent is strong, and several find it greasy or pilling under makeup, especially on oily, acne-prone or hot-climate skin. Reformulation was blamed by some.

Most users find it a reliable, hydrating cream for dry skin that doesn't clog pores, including for acne-prone and sensitive types. One user says the reformulated green-lid version breaks them out, unlike the old one.

Users are divided on this foaming cleanser: many find it gentle and non-stripping, with some calling it a holy grail for sensitive or acne-prone skin. Others found it drying, irritating or breakout-causing, and one disliked the scent.

Most users like it as a gentle makeup remover and cleanser, with some saying it breaks down blackheads without causing breakouts. A few broke out or felt dry and flaky, and one disliked the ginseng scent.

Most users say it removes makeup and sunscreen well and rinses cleanly, with several using it for a year or more. A few find it stings the eyes or struggles with waterproof makeup, and some dislike its waxy smell. Unscented and good value to some.

Most users love this gentle, hydrating cleansing milk, often calling it a holy grail that doesn't leave skin tight, including for rosacea-prone skin. The main concern is spoilage: a few reported a bottle that smelled off, was contaminated or moldy.

Users generally like it as a moisturizer with sun protection that spreads easily and protects well, but opinions are mixed on feel. Some find it greasy, a few see pilling under makeup, and one found the chemical filters bothered their eyes or broke them out.

Users who liked it report faded dark marks and redness, and some find it gentle for sensitive skin. A sizable group, though, broke out, with some getting cystic acne, and one found it drying or irritating.

Several long-term users are happy with it, calling it effective without irritation, though some find the cost hard to sustain. Others got peeling, redness or flakiness, and it proved too strong for one with sensitive skin. A couple saw little change.
Users are mixed. A few long-term users love it, but the strong smell is the main complaint, and several found it sticky, hard to dissolve, quick to oxidize or ineffective on dark marks.

Users who liked the original say it cleared texture and redness, but most reviews here concern the reformulated version, which many found bad smelling, burning or irritating. A couple report pilling or breakouts.

Most users love this hydrating face mist for its fruity scent and glow, using it as a toner layer or setting spray. A few find the smell strong, and a couple had a bottle go dark or rancid, or the spray turn uneven.

Users are split on The INKEY List 10% Azelaic Acid Serum. Fans find it absorbent, soothing and good for redness, rosacea and acne marks, and often prefer its texture to The Ordinary's. Others saw no results, peeling, pilling or a bad breakout, which is the main complaint. Results look unpredictable.

Many users find it hydrating, quick to absorb and gentle, especially on dry or sensitive skin, and good value. The biggest complaint is breakouts and clogged pores, and a fair number find it greasy or heavy. Some say it is not rich enough for winter or very dry skin.

Most users find it light, moisturizing and gentle, with no white cast and little eye stinging compared with other sunscreens. The main downsides are breakouts or closed comedones for some, plus stinging and a greasy, very dewy finish for a few. Oily and acne-prone skin tends to find it heavier.

Many users love it as a thick, basic cream for dry skin and a damaged barrier, and some use it on body and hands. The main complaint is breakouts and closed comedones, especially on oily or acne-prone skin. Some also report burning or irritation, and a few find it too heavy for the face.

Most users find it very gentle and non-stripping, especially on sensitive, rosacea-prone or eczema-prone skin. The main downside is dryness: some feel tight or stripped, and a number get irritation or small bumps. It is basic, so a moisturizer afterward matters.

Most users find it very light, fast-absorbing and less shiny than the original Relief Sun, with no white cast, and it suits oily and combination skin. The main complaint is pilling, mostly when layered with other products or makeup, though many never see it. A few report breakouts or eye stinging.

Users who like it find it hydrating and gentle for dry or sensitive skin. The two biggest complaints are breakouts, including closed comedones and cystic acne, and pilling under sunscreen or makeup. Some also report burning, redness or irritation.

Many users find it a hydrating, gentle, lotion-like moisturizer or sleeping pack for dry skin. The main complaint is breakouts and closed comedones, and many find it greasy or too heavy, especially on oily skin or in summer. Some do better using it only a couple of times a week, and a few report jars going rancid.

Most users find it creamy and very gentle, leaving skin clean and soft without stripping, even on dry or sensitive skin, and a little goes a long way. Downsides are limited: some dislike the fragrance, a few get irritation or breakouts, and some find it not worth the price.

Many users use it a few nights a week for smoother, brighter, more even skin and call it a long-term favorite, with some finding it gentle on sensitive skin. Others see little effect, say results faded over time, or find it pricey for what it does. A few get stinging, breakouts or dislike the smell.

Most users use it as a hydrating, glowy primer or mix it into foundation, and many love the dewy finish. Several doubt it does much for the skin beyond that. Downsides are a candy-like scent, a tacky feel, and irritation or breakouts for some.

Users mostly describe a basic, gentle moisturizer for the eye area that sinks in and sits well under concealer. Many say it hydrates but does little for dark circles or lines. The main downsides are stinging, redness or irritation, and some get pimples or milia under the eyes.

Many users see brighter, more even skin and faded acne marks over a few months, often alongside the matching toner pads, and find it lightweight and non-irritating. Results are slow, and a good number saw no change in dark spots. Some get small bumps or breakouts, and a few dislike the scent.

Most users find it a very hydrating, gentle cream, popular at night for dry skin. Downsides are a tacky or sticky feel, pilling under sunscreen or makeup, and a greasy look on oily skin. A few get irritation or breakouts, and some find it too light for very dry skin.

Many users like it as a hydrating serum with a subtle glow, and some say it helps acne-prone skin calm and heal faster. A sizeable group sees little or no effect beyond hydration, especially for the price. Some find it sticky, and a few get breakouts or irritation.

Many users find it a plain, lightweight, hydrating lotion that suits sensitive, eczema-prone and acne-prone skin. A notable group gets stinging, burning or redness instead, and some break out. A few find it too light for very dry skin in winter.

Most users find it a very gentle, non-stripping cleanser for sensitive skin. The main downside is weak cleansing: many say it leaves a film or does not remove sunscreen or makeup alone, so it suits a mild or second cleanse. Some get stinging, eye irritation or redness.

Users are split. Many like the light foam that cleans and removes makeup without drying. Nearly as many find it drying, stripping or irritating, with stinging, redness or breakouts for some, and a few notice a chemical smell.

Most users like this fragrance-free gel-cream as a light, hydrating, gentle moisturizer, including on sensitive, oily and acne-prone skin. The main downside is that very dry skin or winter often needs something richer. A few get stinging or breakouts, and several say a jar runs out fast.

Most users like it as a clear, primer-like sunscreen with no white cast that sits well under makeup. The silicone texture divides people, and some find it greasy or dislike the feel. Other downsides are eye stinging, pilling for some, and breakouts for a few.

Many users love it as a hydrating yet fairly light cream that sinks in well, including on dry or sensitive skin. The main complaints are pilling under makeup or sunscreen, plus irritation and breakouts for some. Several long-time users say newer tubes and refills are thinner and worse.

Many users say it calms redness, clears pimples and fades marks, often on rosacea or hormonal acne. The main downside is the thick, silicone-like texture, which pills over other products for many and feels gritty to some. A few get irritation or breakouts.

Others say it leaves residue, does not rinse fully, or struggles with sunscreen and waterproof makeup, and a few report tubes smelling off.
